definition_quote.value: 'Practicing medicine' means the diagnosis, treatment, or offer to treat a mental or physical disease or disorder or a physical deformity or injury by any system or method, or the attempt to effect cures of those conditions, by a person who: (A) publicly professes to be a physician or surgeon; or (B) directly or indirectly charges money or other compensation for those services.

drug_authority.value: A physician licensed under this subtitle may supply a patient with any drug, remedy, or clinical supply necessary to meet the patient's immediate needs. Physicians may prescribe, administer, and dispense drugs including controlled substances. Physicians may delegate prescribing authority to advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants through prescriptive authority agreements, subject to statutory limits.
drug_authority.quote: A physician licensed under this subtitle may supply a patient with any drug, remedy, or clinical supply necessary to meet the patient's immediate needs.

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: A license applicant who is a graduate of a medical school located outside the United States and Canada must: (1) be a graduate of a school whose curriculum meets requirements for an unapproved medical school as determined by a committee of experts selected by the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board; (2) have successfully completed at least two years of graduate medical training in the United States or Canada approved by the board; (3) hold a valid certificate issued by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG); and (4) be able to communicate in English.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: holds a valid certificate issued by the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates; and (4) is able to communicate in English.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: The board shall adopt guidelines for the prescription of opioid antagonists. Delegation of controlled substance prescribing to APRNs/PAs is limited: Schedule III-V only (with exceptions for Schedule II in hospital facility-based practice or hospice), prescriptions limited to 90-day supply with refills requiring physician consultation. The board provides information to license holders at least biennially on prescribing pain medications with emphasis on Schedule II and III controlled substances.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: the prescription is for a controlled substance listed in Schedule III, IV, or V as established by the commissioner of the Department of State Health Services under Chapter 481, Health and Safety Code; (2) the prescription, including a refill of the prescription, is for a period not to exceed 90 days;

pain_management_clinic_registration_requ.quote: A pain management clinic may not operate in this state unless the clinic is certified under this chapter.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: A valid practitioner-patient relationship exists for telemedicine if the physician has a preexisting relationship with the patient, communicates pursuant to a call coverage agreement, or provides services through synchronous audiovisual interaction, asynchronous store-and-forward technology, or other audiovisual telecommunication technology, provided the physician complies with the standard of care. A practitioner-patient relationship is not present if a practitioner prescribes an abortifacient or any drug that terminates a pregnancy.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: a valid practitioner-patient relationship is present between a practitioner providing a telemedicine medical service or a teledentistry dental service and a patient receiving the service as long as the practitioner complies with the standard of care described in Section 111.007
telehealth_prescribing_rules.citation: [UMBRELLA / Subtitle A - Provisions Applying to Health Professions Gener] Section 111.005

telemedicine_license_available.quote: A physician must meet the eligibility requirements as defined in Section 171.002(11) to receive an expedited license under the terms and provisions of the compact.

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: the member states of the Interstate Medical Licensure Compact have allied in common purpose to develop a comprehensive process that complements the existing licensing and regulatory authority of state medical boards and provides a streamlined process that allows physicians to become licensed in multiple states

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: A physician may delegate to an advanced practice registered nurse or physician assistant, acting under adequate physician supervision, the act of prescribing or ordering a drug or device as authorized through a prescriptive authority agreement between the physician and the advanced practice registered nurse or physician assistant

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: A physician may delegate to a physician assistant the prescribing or ordering of nonprescription drugs, dangerous drugs, and controlled substances in Schedule III-V (limited to 90-day supply; refills require physician consultation). Schedule II controlled substances may be delegated only in hospital facility-based practice for admitted patients or emergency department patients, or as part of hospice care. Delegation must be through a prescriptive authority agreement.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician's authority to delegate the prescribing or ordering of a drug or device under this subchapter is limited to: (1) nonprescription drugs; (2) dangerous drugs; and (3) controlled substances to the extent provided by Subsections (b) and (b-1).

max_physician_assistants_per_supervising.quote: the combined number of advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants with whom a physician may enter into a prescriptive authority agreement may not exceed seven advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants or the full-time equivalent of seven advanced practice registered nurses and physician assistants.

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: The board shall review the medical competency of a physician against whom three or more expert reports under Section 74.351, Civil Practice and Remedies Code, have been filed in three separate lawsuits within a five-year period

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: A medical peer review committee or health care entity shall report in writing to the board the results and circumstances of a medical peer review that: (1) adversely affects the clinical privileges of a physician for a period longer than 14 days;

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: The Texas Physician Health Program is established to promote: (1) physician and physician assistant wellness; and (2) treatment of all health conditions that have the potential to compromise the physician's or physician assistant's ability to practice with reasonable skill and safety, including mental health issues, substance abuse issues, and addiction issues.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: In enforcing Section 164.051(a)(4), the board, on probable cause, shall request the affected physician or applicant to submit to a mental or physical examination by physicians designated by the board.

administrative_medicine_license_availabl.quote: The board shall adopt rules for the issuance of a license that limits the license holder to the practice of administrative medicine.

The board may adopt rules and prescribe fees related to the issuance of a license under this section that is limited in scope to an applicant by virtue of the applicant's conceded eminence and authority in the applicant's specialty.

The board on majority vote may probate an order canceling, revoking, or suspending a license or imposing any other method of discipline if the probationer conforms to each order, condition, and rule the board establishes as a term of probation.
The board shall suspend a physician's license on proof that the physician has been: (1) initially convicted of: (A) a felony;
On final conviction for an offense described by Subsection (a), the board shall revoke the physician's license.
The board may accept the voluntary surrender of a license.
The board may issue a faculty temporary license to practice medicine to a physician as provided by this section.

The board may issue a military limited volunteer license to practice medicine to an applicant who: (1) is licensed and in good standing, or was licensed and retired in good standing, as a physician in another state;
A physician seeking licensure through the compact shall file an application for an expedited license with the member board of the state selected by the physician as the state of principal license.

The board as provided by board rule may issue a physician-in-training permit to a physician not otherwise licensed by the board who is participating in a graduate medical education training program approved by the board.
